B: Hiya! Ooh, hello! You're Dean, is it?
A: Yeah. Alright. Gillingham.
B: Leanne, Castleford. Kent, is that? I've only been to Kent once, school trip to Canterbury. I were sick on the coach.
A: Ha. Classic.
B: How've your calls been? I've had some lovely ones.
A: Yeah, fine. Had Kerry just now, she's sound. We talked about chips in the car.
B: Oh, Kerry! I haven't had her. I thought she looked dead sweet. So what is it you do?
A: Admin at a plumbing supplies place. Invoices, phones. Coffee machine's broke. That's my life.
B: Oh no, you're not the coffee one, are you? Marisol told me! She said she nearly cried for you.
A: Ha. Yeah. She weren't impressed. Three weeks now.
B: Three weeks! I'd be marching into the office. I'm at a food factory, packing line, I train the new starters. We've got a tea machine and if that broke there'd be a riot.
A: Ours is just everyone moaning and nobody ringing anyone. Including me.
B: Ha! Well, at least you're honest. What do you do when you're not doing invoices?
A: Football mostly. Gillingham, which is a mistake. FIFA. Pub quiz Thursdays.
B: Thursdays! Me too, with work. We're rubbish. Last week we got a whole round on rivers and nobody knew a thing. I should've had Matthew with us, him from Norwich, he does rivers.
A: I just go for the pint really. I'm alright on the sport round.
B: See, you'd be handy. We've got nobody for sport. Well, except rugby, I'm Castleford Tigers. Rugby league. Me and my sister go a few times a season.
A: Oh right. Never really watched rugby league. Any good this year?
B: Don't. Don't get me started. We lost at the weekend and I were proper upset, my sister had to buy me a chippy tea to calm me down.
A: Ha. Same. Gillingham lost Saturday, I moaned at my brother all the way home. He drives, so he can't escape.
B: Ha! Poor lad. Do you go with him every time?
A: Most times. It's the only time we see each other proper, to be honest. He's got a kid now, house, all that.
B: Aw, that's nice though, that you've got that. Football's like that, isn't it, it's not really about the football.
A: Yeah. Suppose. Me and my dad were the same with Chelsea.
B: My dad were rugby mad. He used to take me when I were little, I didn't have a clue what was going on, I just had a pie. He's passed now. Oh, here I go, sorry.
A: No, you're alright. Sorry about your dad.
B: Thanks, love. It's a while ago. Right, what are you having for your tea tonight? I ask everybody.
A: Dinner? Probably chicken in the air fryer. Oven chips. Jade, my girlfriend, she's doing it, so whatever she says really.
